Not measured. CuBi2O4 usually behaves as a p-type photocathode, so it is unlikely to be a good photoanode.

content.text:
I submitted **index 56** (Bi 0.09, Cu 0.44, V 0.46). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, at **1.34 µA**. I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases below are inferred from composition, not confirmed.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Likely phase region | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.36 / 0.21 / 0.43 | BiVO4-like, with some Cu | 0.90 µA |
| **56** | 0.09 / 0.44 / 0.46 | Copper vanadate, Cu:V about 1:1 (β-Cu2V2O7-like) | **1.34 µA** |
| 50 | 0.09 / 0.58 / 0.34 | Copper vanadate with extra Cu (Cu3V2O8-like) | 0.53 µA |

- **Why these three:** with only three measurements I sampled three different phase regions rather than trying to refine within one. BiVO4's band gap sits close to the 2.4 eV illumination, so it absorbs only weakly. Copper vanadates have gaps around 2 eV and absorb much more strongly.
- **What the results suggest:** the 1:1 copper-vanadate region did best, and adding more Cu (index 50) cut the photocurrent by more than half.
- **Not tested:** I skipped the Bi-rich CuBi2O4 region, such as indices 103 and 173. That material usually behaves as a photocathode, so it's unlikely to be a good photoanode.

I can't tell whether 56 is the best composition in the library, because the neighbouring Cu:V ≈ 1 compositions (for example 27, 39, 60 and 111) were never measured. The best candidate could be anywhere between those points and 56.
